target_customer: AI platforms and developers whose agents need to pay for APIs and services under spending limits
problem: Autonomous agents need to transact for data and services, but businesses need permissions, limits and audit trails on every payment.
business_model: Usage-based payments and API billing layer plus subscription tiers (Free, $200 and $1,000 per month)

founders.name: Cole Dermott
founders.background_notes: YC page bio is only 'I like moving money'; employers and education not listed on the page.

competitors.name: Skyfire
competitors.what: Wallet and payment network that lets AI agents spend money

technical_complexity.rationale: Non custodial wallets, USDC settlement, spending policy engine and metering across many APIs; hard parts are security and compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Integration into platform billing gives some stickiness but protocols like x402 and several funded rivals make the space contested.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Many agent payment offerings appeared during 2025 and 2026; Locus remained independent and active as of 2026-11.

market_need_then: Agents were moving from tools to autonomous actors in 2025, creating demand for controlled payment rails; evidence is the company's own framing and the number of entrants.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, short imperative lines such as Integrate once. Bill every call.

branding.brand_signature: Product names Pay With Locus, Build With Locus, Checkout With Locus

brand_strength.rationale: Name is shared with several unrelated companies named Locus, which causes confusion in funding databases; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Locus is an early stage, active company. It started with agent wallets and later added an API billing layer reported by RuntimeWire, widening scope toward platforms. No outcome yet; funding beyond the YC investment is not verified and competition in agent payments is dense.
notes: Aggregators report a $0.5M YC convertible note (CB Insights, 2025-10) or $500K pre-seed (VCBacked, Synaptic); only aggregators, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Other aggregators list $8M, $79M and $212M which belong to different companies named Locus. Eliot Lee is named as co-founder by search summaries but not on the YC page, so not listed. A Locus logistics company was acquired by Ingka in 2025, unrelated.
